This investigation will be conducted by a certified home tutor, who agreed to 
allocate three minutes at the beginning of each session for this study. While 
addressing the research objective and selecting a methodology, it is of 
paramount importance to select an approach that matches the studies needs, 
and the complexity of the e-learning application. This section will delineate the 
rationale behind the chosen methodology. 
Surveys offer a pivotal methodology for measuring a student’s perception on 
their level of engagement and learning. Their adaptable nature enables the 
exploration of the students’ subjective opinions related to the applications 
feature set. Despite this, surveys have an inherent bias due to students 
reporting on themselves; while personal experiences are important, objective 
data is needed for a more holistic and accurate view. 
Experiments in controlled settings are an effective approach at demonstrating 
causality between the applications usage and student outcomes. This approach 
allows for the close examination of spaced-repetition and short-form content on 
subject mastery and engagement, providing empirical evidence towards the 
hypothesis. However, given the short time allocation at the start of each lesson,
